q: What should you create to meet requirement 1?
opts: A Microsoft 365 group with assigned membership
An administrative unit for the Sales department
A security group with dynamic user membership based on user.department
A security group with assigned membership, updated by a Logic App
exp: A dynamic user group with a rule such as user.department -eq "Sales" adds and removes members automatically. Contoso already has Entra ID P1, which dynamic groups require. A Logic App works but adds administrative effort.

q: Which role assignment meets requirement 2?
opts: Owner at the Sub-Dev scope
Contributor at the Sub-Dev scope
Contributor at the MG-Contoso scope
User Access Administrator at the Sub-Dev scope
exp: Contributor can manage every resource but cannot assign roles. Scoping it to Sub-Dev limits it to development; MG-Contoso would also cover Sub-Prod. Owner and User Access Administrator can grant access.

q: Complete the statement to meet requirement 3.
exp: The built-in Allowed locations policy (Deny) blocks other regions. Assigning it at MG-Contoso covers both subscriptions and any subscription added under that management group later, with a single assignment.

q: What should you configure to meet requirement 4?
opts: A ReadOnly lock on RG-Core
An Azure Policy with the Deny effect on RG-Core
A CanNotDelete lock on RG-Core
Remove the Owner role from all administrators
exp: A CanNotDelete lock on RG-Core stops anyone deleting the resource group or anything in it, while still allowing changes. A ReadOnly lock would also block configuration changes. A Deny policy doesn't control deletes, and removing every Owner role would stop admins doing their jobs.

q: For requirement 5, answer Yes or No:
stmts: Contoso's current licensing supports password writeback
Password writeback must be enabled in Microsoft Entra Connect
Security questions must be enabled as an SSPR method for writeback to work
Password writeback requires Microsoft Entra ID P2
exp: Writeback needs Entra ID P1 or higher (Contoso has P1) and must be enabled in Entra Connect and in the Password reset settings. It does not depend on security questions, and P2 is not required.

q: How should you give the auditor access (requirement 4)?
opts: Create a member account auditor@fabrikam.com and assign Reader on Sub1
Invite the auditor as a B2B guest and assign Reader on Sub1
Invite the auditor as a B2B guest and assign Contributor on Sub1
Share the subscription owner's credentials for the audit period
exp: Invite the auditor as a B2B guest, so they sign in with their own organisation's account and you don't manage a password. Assign Reader on Sub1 so they can view but not change. A member account would mean managing their credentials, Contributor gives too much access, and sharing credentials is never acceptable.

q: Complete the role assignment for WebOps (requirement 1).
exp: Virtual Machine Contributor lets WebOps manage VMs (create, start, stop, resize) but not the virtual networks or storage accounts they connect to, and it can't assign roles. Assigning it at RG-Web scope keeps WebOps out of the other resource groups.

q: Which role should the DBA team get (requirement 2)?
opts: Contributor on RG-Data
Owner on RG-Data
User Access Administrator on Sub1
Contributor on Sub1
exp: Owner gives full control of the resources and lets the team assign roles to junior DBAs. Contributor cannot assign roles; anything at Sub1 scope is broader than needed.

q: Which role should Finance get (requirement 3)?
opts: Billing Reader
Reader
Contributor
Cost Management Contributor
exp: Cost Management Contributor can view costs and manage budgets and other cost configuration without managing resources. Billing Reader and Reader cannot create budgets.

q: For requirements 5 and 6, answer Yes or No:
stmts: A budget with an 80% alert condition stops resources when the threshold is reached
The built-in policy "Require a tag on resource groups" with the Deny effect meets requirement 6
Tags on a resource group are inherited automatically by the resources inside it
A budget alert can trigger an action group as well as send email
exp: Budgets only notify; they never stop resources. The Require-a-tag policy with Deny blocks resource groups without the tag. Tags are not inherited by default. Budget alerts can call action groups.

q: Complete the command so user1 can view all resources in resource group RG1 only.
exp: Reader grants view-only access. The resource group scope is the full path /subscriptions/<id>/resourceGroups/RG1 (you could also use --resource-group RG1). The subscription scope would be too broad.

q: Complete the command to stop anyone deleting RG1 while still allowing changes.
exp: In PowerShell, CLI and the API, the lock that blocks deletes is called CanNotDelete (the portal shows it as 'Delete'). It still allows changes to the resource group. ReadOnly would block changes too.

q: Choose the policy effect for each goal.
tpl:
Block VMs with sizes that are not allowed: [[0]]
Only report storage accounts without HTTPS-only: [[1]]
Add a missing tag while resources are created or updated: [[2]]
exp: Deny blocks non-compliant requests, Audit only reports, and Modify adds or changes properties such as tags during create or update. DeployIfNotExists deploys a related resource.

q: Choose the minimum licence for each feature.
tpl:
Dynamic membership groups: [[0]]
Privileged Identity Management: [[1]]
Conditional Access: [[2]]
exp: Dynamic membership groups need Microsoft Entra ID P1, because group rules are a premium feature. Conditional Access also needs P1. Privileged Identity Management (just-in-time, approval-based admin roles) needs P2 or Entra ID Governance. The Free edition includes neither dynamic groups nor Conditional Access.

q: Complete the custom role so it can view VMs and restart them, and can be assigned anywhere in one subscription.
exp: The read action lets the role see VMs; the restart action allows restarts. Microsoft.Compute/* or * would grant far more. Custom roles cannot use the root scope "/"; a subscription ID is a valid assignable scope.

q: Complete the SSPR registration settings.
tpl: To make users register their methods at next sign-in, set "Require users to register when signing in" to [[0]]. By default, users are asked to reconfirm their information every [[1]] days.
exp: Setting 'Require users to register when signing in' to Yes prompts users to register their SSPR methods at sign-in. 'Number of days before users are asked to re-confirm their authentication information' defaults to 180 days, so users check their details are still correct twice a year.

q: Complete the dynamic membership rule to include Sales department users whose licence usage location is Pakistan.
exp: department holds the department name. usageLocation is the two-letter country code used for licensing (PK). The country attribute is free text such as "Pakistan".

q: Complete the commands to create a management group and place Sub1 under it.
tpl:
az account management-group [[0]] --name MG-Prod
az account management-group subscription [[1]] --name MG-Prod --subscription Sub1
exp: az account management-group create creates a new management group. az account management-group subscription add then moves a subscription under it. The subscription inherits the group's RBAC assignments and policies.

q: Complete the command so env=prod is added to RG1 without removing its existing tags.
exp: az tag update --operation Merge adds or updates the tags you specify and keeps every other tag. Replace would remove any tag not in the list, and Delete removes the specified tags.

q: Complete the statement.
tpl: To stop ordinary members from inviting guests, change [[0]] in [[1]].
exp: Who can invite guests is set in Microsoft Entra ID → External Identities → External collaboration settings, under Guest invite settings. You can allow anyone, members only, only admins and the Guest Inviter role, or nobody.

q: Match each requirement to the Azure feature that meets it.
items: Prevent deletion of a resource group
Apply governance to many subscriptions at once
Restrict which regions resources can use
exp: Tags group costs; locks prevent deletion; management groups organise subscriptions for inherited governance; Azure Policy restricts properties such as location.

q: Match each description to the built-in role.
exp: Contributor manages all resources but can't grant access. User Access Administrator manages access but not resources. Reader can only view. Owner can do both — manage resources and grant access.

q: Match each feature to the minimum Microsoft Entra licence.
exp: Conditional Access and group-based licensing need Microsoft Entra ID P1. Privileged Identity Management and Identity Protection's risk-based policies need P2. Basic user and group management is included in the Free tier.

q: Match each device to the right Microsoft Entra device identity.
items: Corporate PC already joined to on-premises AD
exp: A corporate PC already joined to on-premises AD becomes Microsoft Entra hybrid joined, so it's known to both. An employee's personal phone is Microsoft Entra registered (BYOD). A new cloud-only corporate laptop is Microsoft Entra joined.

q: Match each behaviour to the Azure Policy effect.
items: Deploys a related resource when it is missing
exp: Deny blocks a non-compliant create or update request. Audit allows it but reports it as non-compliant. Modify adds or changes properties (such as tags) during deployment. DeployIfNotExists deploys a missing related resource after the main resource is created.

q: Match each task to the least-privileged Microsoft Entra role.
exp: Application Administrator manages apps; Global Administrator has full control; Helpdesk Administrator resets non-admin passwords; User Administrator creates users and groups.

q: Match each description to the identity type.
items: Deleted automatically with its Azure resource
Standalone and can be shared by several resources
targets: Service principal with a client secret
exp: Guests are invited external users. A system-assigned identity shares its resource's lifecycle. A user-assigned identity is its own resource and can be attached to many resources.

q: Match each need to the cost tool.
items: Get right-sizing recommendations for idle VMs
Analyse what you actually spent last month
Estimate the cost of a planned deployment
exp: Advisor recommends savings; Cost analysis shows actual spend; the pricing calculator estimates new deployments; the TCO calculator compares on-premises with Azure.

code:
Principal            Role         Scope
-------------------  -----------  ----------------------------------------
user1@contoso.com    Reader       /subscriptions/1111
Ops-Group            Contributor  /subscriptions/1111/resourceGroups/RG1
q: user1 is a member of Ops-Group. What can user1 do in resource group RG2 (in the same subscription)?
opts: Create, change and delete resources
Only view resources
Nothing
Assign roles to other users
exp: In RG2 the only assignment that applies is Reader at the subscription scope, which is inherited by every resource group, so user1 can view but not change anything. The Contributor assignment applies only to RG1. Neither role lets user1 assign roles.

q: Review the custom role. Answer Yes or No for a user who has ONLY this role:
stmts: The user can create storage accounts
The user can delete storage accounts
The user can read blob contents using Microsoft Entra authorisation
The role can be assigned to a resource group in subscription 1111
exp: storageAccounts/* includes write (create and update), but NotActions removes delete. There are no DataActions, so no blob data access. A resource group inside the assignable subscription is a valid scope.

q: This policy is assigned to a subscription with allowedLocations = ["westeurope", "northeurope"]. What happens when someone deploys a VM to East US?
opts: The VM is created and flagged as non-compliant
The VM is created and moved to West Europe
The deployment is denied
The VM is created and tagged with the allowed locations
exp: The policy rule matches any resource whose location isn't in the allowed list and applies the Deny effect. East US isn't in [westeurope, northeurope], so the deployment request is rejected before anything is created. Policy never moves or tags resources in this case.

q: The same deny policy is assigned today. A storage account was created in East US last month. What happens to it?
opts: It is deleted at the next evaluation
It keeps running and is reported as non-compliant
It is stopped
It is moved to West Europe automatically
exp: Deny only blocks new create and update requests. Existing resources are still evaluated and appear as non-compliant in the compliance report, but Azure Policy doesn't delete, stop or move them. You'd have to fix them yourself (Deny has no remediation).

q: This Bicep file is deployed to resource group RG-Prod. An administrator then tries to scale out an App Service plan in RG-Prod. What happens?
opts: The scale-out succeeds because locks only block deletion
The scale-out fails because ReadOnly blocks all write operations
The scale-out succeeds for Owners only
The lock is removed automatically
exp: A ReadOnly lock at the resource group scope applies to every resource in it and blocks all write operations, including scaling, for everyone until the lock is removed.

q: Which user becomes a member of the group with this dynamic rule?
opts: department "IT Operations", jobTitle "Manager"
department "Finance", jobTitle "Analyst"
department "HR", jobTitle "Senior Engineer"
department "Sales", jobTitle "Account Manager"
exp: The rule uses -or, so a user matching either condition joins. -contains is a substring match, so jobTitle "Senior Engineer" contains "Engineer" and matches. The department condition uses -eq, which needs an exact match, so "IT Operations" doesn't equal "IT".

code:
AzureActivity
| where OperationNameValue == "MICROSOFT.AUTHORIZATION/ROLEASSIGNMENTS/WRITE"
| where ActivityStatusValue == "Success"
| project TimeGenerated, Caller, ResourceGroup
q: What does this Log Analytics query return?
opts: Every failed sign-in to the tenant, with the user name and the IP address
Successful role assignment creations, with who made them and where
All users who have the Owner role
Resource locks that were removed
exp: Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write is the operation recorded when someone creates a role assignment. The query keeps only successful ones and shows the time, the caller (who did it) and the resource group. It doesn't cover sign-ins, existing role holders or lock removals.

code:
Tenant Root Group
└── MG-Corp        (Policy: Allowed locations = westeurope)
    ├── MG-Prod    (RBAC: Ops-Group = Contributor)
    │   └── Sub-Prod
    └── MG-Dev
        └── Sub-Dev
q: Review the hierarchy and its assignments. Answer Yes or No:
stmts: The Allowed locations policy applies to Sub-Dev
Ops-Group can create resources in Sub-Dev
Ops-Group can create resources in Sub-Prod in West Europe
A new subscription moved under MG-Prod gets both the policy and the role assignment
exp: Policy and RBAC assignments inherit down the hierarchy. MG-Corp's policy reaches both subscriptions. Ops-Group's Contributor role is on MG-Prod only, so it covers Sub-Prod and any subscription later placed under MG-Prod.

q: A monthly budget of 1,000 USD has these notifications. Actual spend is 600 USD, but Azure forecasts 1,150 USD for the month. What happens?
opts: Nothing until actual spend passes 800 USD
An email is sent because forecasted spend is above 100% of the budget
Resources are stopped when the forecast passes 1,000 USD
Both notifications fire at the end of the month only
exp: A forecasted notification fires as soon as Azure predicts spend will reach its threshold by the end of the period, even though actual spend is lower. The forecast of 1,150 USD is over 100% of the 1,000 USD budget, so the email goes out now. Budgets never stop resources.

q: After this command runs, what can members of the group do?
opts: Manage VMs in RG-App, but not the virtual networks they connect to, and not assign roles
Manage every resource in RG-App
Manage VMs and their virtual networks in RG-App, and assign VM roles to others
Only start and stop VMs in RG-App
exp: Virtual Machine Contributor lets the group manage VMs — create, start, stop, resize and delete — but not the virtual networks or storage accounts the VMs use, and it can't assign roles. The command's scope is RG-App, so it doesn't apply to other resource groups.

stmts: Sara signs in with her Fabrikam credentials

code:
az policy assignment create --name inherit-costcenter \
  --policy <id of "Inherit a tag from the resource group"> \
  --scope /subscriptions/1111 \
  --mi-system-assigned --location westeurope \
  --params '{ "tagName": { "value": "costcenter" } }'
q: Why does this policy assignment include a managed identity?
opts: Policy assignments always need an identity
The Modify effect needs an identity to change tags on existing resources through remediation
The identity is needed to read the tag value from the resource group
The Modify effect needs an identity so that it can bypass resource locks during remediation
exp: "Inherit a tag from the resource group" uses the Modify effect. Remediation tasks change existing resources by acting as the assignment's managed identity, which needs a role such as Tag Contributor.
